items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Because what we played on those records was our, the white man's impression, of what King Oliver and Louis were doing.

ctx.x: Now, to get back to the black business again. I think that I learned more actually from the black dancers and black singers such as Ethel Waters and Bessie Smith than I did from black players, but the strange thing about it all was that I was not influenced by one kind of jazz. For instance, the first time I heard Coleman Hawkins play, I was amazed to hear the powerful authority this man had on the tenor because in those days, tenor was played as an accompanimental instrument. I was supposed to be the first white…

But I would like to think that King Oliver and Louis started the so-called Chicago Jazz. Because what we played on those records was our, the white man's impression, of what King Oliver and Louis were doing.
